questions.question: Which is the most natural English translation of today's [ZH] line: "把git的状态都调整好,接下来要开始大量的写代码了"?
options: A. Get the git status sorted out — we're about to start writing a lot of code.
B. Adjust all git status good, next will start write many code.
C. Make git state all correct, then begin to do large amount coding.
D. Fix the git situations, after that we will start massive write codes.
questions.explanation: 调整好 means get things sorted out or cleaned up. 大量的写代码 means writing a lot of code — option A is natural and matches a pre-refactor workflow.

questions.question: How do you best express today's architecture decision: "middleware-service 只提供能力，edge-agent 负责编排"?
options: A. middleware-service only provides capabilities; edge-agent handles orchestration.
B. middleware-service only give ability, edge-agent responsible arrange.
C. middleware-service just offer powers, edge-agent do the compose work.
D. middleware-service provides all, edge-agent only orchestrate the middle.
questions.explanation: 能力 is capabilities (not generic 'ability'), and 编排 is orchestration — the division of responsibility between middleware and edge-agent.

questions.question: In today's [EN] entry you wrote "go ahead." What does this most naturally mean in a coding session?
options: A. Proceed — continue with the planned work.
B. Go to the front of the line.
C. Move ahead in the git history.
D. Run the program forward.
questions.explanation: "Go ahead" is a common confirmation meaning proceed or continue — you used it to green-light the next step in the edge-agent refactor.

questions.question: Which sentence best matches today's [EN] instruction "generate the Stage-0 skeleton code"?
options: A. Generate the Stage-0 skeleton code.
B. Generate the stage zero skeleton codes.
C. Create the Stage-0 frame code structure.
D. Make skeleton for stage 0 coding.
questions.explanation: Your original phrasing is already correct. 'Skeleton code' is standard for scaffold/stub implementations; Stage-0 keeps the hyphenated project phase name.

questions.question: Which English phrase best translates the design principle from today's [ZH] line: "按模块把, 也不要切的过细, 要高内聚低耦合"?
options: A. Organize by module — don't split too finely; aim for high cohesion and low coupling.
B. By module cut, not too thin, need high inside gather low mix.
C. Split by modules but not over small, want high cohesion and low couple.
D. Module by module, avoid too fine, high gather inside and low connect outside.
questions.explanation: 高内聚低耦合 is the standard software-design phrase high cohesion and low coupling. 不要切的过细 warns against over-fragmenting modules.

questions.question: Which question best matches today's [EN] line: "So, I can tell codex to implement the code on the left now?"
options: A. So, can I tell Codex to implement the code on the left now?
B. So, I can tell codex implement the left side code now?
C. So, should I let codex to do the left code implementation now?
D. So, I can say codex implement left code now, right?
questions.explanation: Your sentence is already natural. Option A only adds a question mark and capitalizes Codex — confirming you're ready to hand off implementation to the AI agent.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "这个项目已经不是POC MVP这个, 项目有体现把"
questions.modelAnswer: This project is no longer a POC or MVP — the codebase should reflect that.
questions.explanation: POC (proof of concept) and MVP (minimum viable product) are left as acronyms. 有体现 means the project itself should show or reflect the mature stage.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "给我一个整体的架构图,给我看看"
questions.modelAnswer: Give me an overall architecture diagram — I want to take a look.
questions.explanation: 整体的架构图 is an overall/high-level architecture diagram. The trailing 给我看看 softens the request: let me see it / I want to review it.

questions.question: Translate into natural English for a design-doc workflow: "写进文档,结构图放 SSOT §1,运行时图放 §4"
questions.modelAnswer: Write it into the doc — put the structure diagram in SSOT §1 and the runtime diagram in §4.
questions.explanation: 写进文档 means commit the content to the documentation. SSOT (single source of truth) section references stay as written in technical docs.

questions.question: Rewrite today's [EN] line as a clear commit instruction: "commit this and add the config scaffolding"
questions.modelAnswer: Commit this and add the config scaffolding.
questions.explanation: Your original line is already a natural commit instruction. 'Config scaffolding' means the initial config file structure needed before full implementation.
